items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: that Hank O'Neal who recorded and produced it wrote down

ctx.x: Now the songs, just to make sure, are Fidgety Feet, 'Baby Won't You Please Come Home,' 'Wait on the New Orleans,' 'Tin Blues,' 'Sweet Georgia Brown,' 'After You've Gone,' New Orleans, 'Struttin' at the Barbecue,' 'Basin Street Blues' and 'Wolverine Blues.'

And there are some most interesting notes here, that Hank O'Neal who recorded and produced it wrote down. It starts off -- and I'm only going to take a couple of them here -- "I hate Dixieland jazz, at least I hate the kind of rubbish people play." In '77, they called it Dixieland.
Later on, he goes on to say "Why am I putting out an album with all these Dixieland tunes on it?" A good question, and an easy answer. It isn't Dixieland. Thank
